scenes.headline: How rotating a vector makes it easy to quantize
scenes.sub: TurboQuant: a data-free quantizer for the KV cache.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Almond! The KV cache caps how much context you can serve. TurboQuant shrinks it: rotate, then quantize.

scenes.label: The idea
scenes.text: Rotate every vector by a random orthogonal matrix first. Its coordinates then follow a known distribution, so one quantizer, solved ahead of time, fits every vector.

steps.label: A few outlier channels carry the magnitude
steps.say: Keys and values have outliers: a few channels carry most of the magnitude. Fixed levels clip them, or waste precision on the empty middle.

steps.label: Online: new tokens, no calibration set
steps.say: Calibrating each channel needs sample data, and online, with new tokens streaming in, there isn't any.

steps.label: After rotation: energy spread evenly
steps.say: Rotate first. Lengths and inner products stay the same, but the energy spreads evenly, and nothing is left to clip.
Each new key is rotated as it arrives.
Its coordinates now follow a known Beta distribution, so the optimal Lloyd-Max levels were solved once, ahead of time. No calibration.
But attention takes inner products, and that quantizer is biased on them. So TurboQuant stores one more bit: the residual's sign, under a random projection.
Together they give an unbiased estimate of query dot key: quality neutral at three and a half bits per channel, the paper reports.

scenes.label: max context in tokens, dense model, on a 4-GPU RTX 5090 box
scenes.note: throughput barely moves: a memory win, not a speed one
scenes.say: In one vLLM build, keys get three bits and values two or four. Max context doubles, while throughput barely moves: a memory win, not a speed one.

scenes.text: Don't fight outliers or calibrate: rotate the data into a known distribution, and the optimal quantizer is solved once.
scenes.mark: rotate the data into a known distribution

recap: A random rotation spreads out the outliers
One Lloyd-Max quantizer, solved ahead of time
A 1-bit residual sign keeps scores unbiased
scenes.say: To recap: rotate, quantize with a precomputed table, and add one bit to stay unbiased.
